en: Regarding the method for the accomplishment of siddhi through the practice of Mahācakra-vajra and its ritual offerings,
I shall briefly describe the sequence of the recitation of Mahācakra based on the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*. First, one should maintain [the practice].
First, purify a chamber;
adorn the site of practice (maṇḍala), construct a maṇḍala,
and burn incense and scatter flowers, along with floral banners, pennants, and canopies.
First, one must receive the empowerment from a teacher;
only after that may one personally receive and maintain the teachings for recitation and practice.
One should perform this three times daily, with one thousand and eighty recitations at each session.
Without shifting or changing [the visualization], once the count reaches three lakṣas, one will immediately attain accomplishment.
Whenever one wishes to enter the maṇḍala,
first visualize the syllable HŪṂ within the mind.
Visualize that the syllable transforms into a great vajra;
then, proceed into the maṇḍala and stand before the principal deity.
With body upright and straight, join your palms and, with a sincere heart, repent and contemplate.
Since beginningless time,
we have wandered through birth and death, failing to awaken to the True Principle and remaining constantly within the three realms.
I now repent of all my karmic obstacles and vow that they shall be entirely extinguished.
The mantra for repentance to eliminate transgressions is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatrapadaviśodhana hana vajraya svāhā. By the power of empowerment through the recitation of this mantra, [the sins are purified].
One attains the Samādhi of the Purity of the Three Karmas.
Next, one should join the palms above the head and recite the mantra for universally prostrating to all Buddhas and the assembly of noble ones.
I say:
Homage to the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the ten directions, who possess the three bodies throughout the three periods of time;
homage to all Mahāyāna teachings; homage to the assembly of non-regressing bodhisattvas.
Homage to all mantras of true reality! Homage to all secret mudrās!
May you, out of compassion, protect and mind me; pull me out from the mire of birth and death.
My fleshly eyes do not see or know, but the Dharma-eye sees everywhere; I take refuge in you.
The mantra for taking refuge is as follows:
Throughout the cycle of birth and death since past lives,
I have acted as I pleased with my body, speech, and mind, And have been possessed by envy and stinginess.
Because my mind was shrouded by wrong views, I have transgressed the samaya; now,
before the Great Holy Honored One, I repent with all my heart,
just as the Buddhas of the past repented, and I do so now in the same way.
May all sentient beings be completely purified by the power of empowerment;
Join the two palms with hollowed palms, Visualize the body as being like lapis lazuli,
Utterly transparent and luminous within and without, By means of the three secrets of the Vajra.
Empower yourself as the Honored One.
Next, with the Seal for Purifying the Three Karmas, apply it to the five locations. The mantra for the rite of pure ablution is as follows:

Placing the vajra-palms upon the crown of the head, one directs the mind throughout the entire dharma-realm to face the Buddhas of the ten directions. Together with the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Vajra-holders,
I purify this body, freeing it from all defilements, as well as the body, speech, and mind of the three periods of time.
Exceeding in number the atoms within the oceans of buddha-fields, [one should] offer them to all the Tathāgatas.
The secret mantra says:
Sitting upright with body and mind clarified, contemplate the *iṣṭadevatā* with focused mindfulness.
First, bind the samaya: join the hands of concentration and wisdom with palms hollowed;
place the thumbs (vīrya) upon the ring fingers (praṇidhāna).
Press the first joints of the back [fingers] with the tips (mudrā), and join the thumbs (vīrya) to the ring fingers (praṇidhāna); pinch the lower joints of each.
Contemplate all the Tathāgatas clearly, with their marks and signs fully manifest.
The Samaya-mantra of the Buddha Family is recited seven times while scattering [the flowers] upon the crown of the head; by this, they are awakened.
The Buddhas come to protect and mindfully hold [the practitioner], Attaining purity of physical action.
Next, present the Lotus Family: As before, join the two palms and extend the remaining six fingers;
Slightly bend them to form an eight-petaled lotus.
Mentally visualize Avalokiteśvara, whose physical marks and signs are most sublime and majestic,
surrounded by an immeasurable koṭi of holy beings of the Lotus family;
through their empowerment, one attains purity of verbal action.
The mantra is: *Vajrasamaya*.
With the left hand covering and the right hand facing upward, join the backs of the fingers together;
[place] the *dāna* and *prajñā* [fingers] together with the *dhyāna* and *upāya* [fingers].
Each [hand] should have the fingers crossed back-to-back; the rest is as for the three-pronged vajra.
One should visualize the Vajragarbha, blazing with wrathful light;
one should examine the Vajra family, surrounded by its own retinue.
By virtue of this empowerment, the mantra for attaining purity of mental action is as follows:
Next, one should don the armor, with the hands of merit and wisdom crossed within.
The fingers of patience and aspiration are joined upright; the fingers of diligence and power are bent like hooks.
The fingers of meditation and wisdom press down upon the square of morality.
Forming this seal at the five locations, it becomes armor that pervades all sentient beings, swiftly causing them to be free from obstacles and hardships.
Neither the various māras nor evil persons shall be able to find an opportunity against him.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the earth-boundary mudrā using the two fingers of the śīla (vow) and kṣānti (patience) families.
Place them in the space between the palms;
with the thumbs and wisdom fingers extended, join the meditation and wisdom fingers together like a vajra,
and press the meditation and wisdom fingers against the ground.
Through the empowerment of the mudrā and mantra, from the base down to the vajra-circle,
a firm boundary is established; the adamantine indestructible seat cannot be moved by celestial māras, and all impurities are transformed into purity.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Vajra Wall. Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā, open the palms and extend the *śamatha* (thumb) and *prajñā* (middle finger). From this mudrā, blazing flames flow forth.
Circumambulate three times clockwise; the mantra for establishing the firm boundary is as follows.
Next, form the Secret Seal of Turning the Wheel of Dharma, which is accomplished merely by the initial resolve.

Each forms the vajra-fist; with the thumb, ring finger, middle finger, and wisdom finger as hooks, through this empowerment, the vessel of the body becomes pure and the Dharma-maṇḍala is accomplished.
One touches the maṇḍala with the mudrā.
One immediately becomes the Vajra Family. By touching the image of the Honored One with the mudrā of the Taming Maṇḍala, or by placing it in the midst of space, all become the maṇḍala.
If the practitioner should transgress the ritual procedure, [the result will not be achieved].
For the purification of the precepts through the power of mantra-empowerment when the samaya has been mistakenly violated, the mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the vast offering mudrā of Ākāśagarbha.
One should join the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, with the *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers interlaced outwardly;
the *vajra*, *maṇi*, and jewel seals flow forth as clouds of all offerings,
including garments, food, drink, palaces, and pavilions.
With clouds and oceans of incense, flowers, music, and various jeweled banners and pennants pervading the ten directions, one truly accomplishes offerings identical to the realm of Sukhāvatī;
in the center of the mandala is the syllable formed by the union of *ḍhri* and *li*.
He emits a great radiance, like the color of red crystal,
Which shines universally throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Those who encounter this light have their karmic obstructions entirely eliminated, Through the power of my merit.
The mantra for abiding while making universal offerings through the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment and the power of the Dharma-realm is as follows:
Next, form the chariot seal (ratha-mudrā) by interlacing the two palms with the fingers facing upward.
Each, by means of dhyāna and prajñā, forms the lower joint of the fingers of the *jñāna-muṣṭi* (wisdom-fist) mudrā;
thus the seven-jeweled chariot is completed.
Proceeding to that Vajra Palace, they invite the Honored One and his retinue, mounting this precious chariot.
The mantra for sending forth the carriage is as follows:
Without releasing the previous mudrā, one should direct the dhyāna and prajñā fingers toward the body and push forward with vigor; thus, the invitation of the carriage is accomplished.
The mantra says:
"The chariot abides in the void; one should welcome the assembly of all the sages.
The inner fist of merit and wisdom has the form of a hook of Prajñāpāramitā."
Having thus made three requests to the body [of the deity], the principal deity and their retinue do not forsake their original vow;
they respond to the invitation and descend into the ritual arena.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Trailokyavijaya (Subduer of the Three Worlds) Wrathful Vajra Mudrā:
with both hands in vajra-fists, hook the thumbs and wisdom fingers together with the right over the left;
extend the forefingers upright at the heart. Visualize that one has become the Principal Deity.
The right foot treads upon Mahādeva; the left treads upon Umādevī.
His entire body blazes with fierce flames. Forming the mudrā by circling counter-clockwise from the heart, forehead, throat, and crown, one performs the ritual of expulsion;
turning clockwise, one firmly establishes the boundary of the camp.
Fierce on all four sides, with eight arms holding various implements and weapons,
standing in the *tiryag* (L-shaped) posture; entering this samādhi,
one should abide in the bodhicitta and give rise to profound compassion.
The mantra for eliminating internal and external obstacles is as follows:
The Vajra Net of the Upper Direction. This is the same mudrā as the earth-element seal previously mentioned;
join the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *anāmikā* (ring finger) of the wisdom-hand with the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* of the action-hand, and rotate it three times above the crown of the head.
The mantra of the Vajra-dṛḍha-jāla is as follows:

Vajra-fire enclosure boundary. With the left hand covering the right, the back of the hands joined, the thumbs and ring fingers extended upward, and the middle fingers and little fingers held in the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* mudrās; one should visualize the flames blazing intensely.
From the seal, light rays stream forth, circling clockwise outside the wall within three layers of flaming enclosures;
even the hosts of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress these, let alone the gods and māras.
The mantra for subduing those who approach is as follows.
Next, perform the *argha* mudrā; visualize bathing the feet of the assembly of noble ones, whereby the practitioner shall attain purity of the three karmas.
The mantra is as follows:

Again, offer a lotus seat; join the palms, extending the fingers of the *śīla* (vow) direction and the *kṣānti* (patience), *praṇidhāna* (vow), and *vīrya* (diligence) directions, so that they are rounded like an eight-petaled lotus.
Visualize that [the mantra] flows forth from the mudrā, and offer immeasurable vajra-flowers to all the Honored Ones.
The mantra is: Oṃ, Mahā-amogharāja, maṇi-pūjā-mudrā.
Joining the vajra palms, with the forefingers pressed together like a jewel,
as soon as one recites the secret mantra, great offerings—
clouds of scented unguents and flower garlands— rain down everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Clouds of burning incense and robes; clouds of mani-luminous lamps, banners, flags, and precious canopies;
with various celestial music pervading all Buddha-fields—truly these constitute offerings.
One shall obtain an immeasurable mass of merit;
like the boundless sky, one shall be constantly born in the assemblies of all Buddhas. The mantra for rescuing and liberating all sentient beings is as follows:
Focus single-mindedly on the deity, Clearly manifest before one’s eyes with compassionate and wrathful features, Surrounded by his retinue;
with every thought, generate yearning devotion, And you shall attain samādhi in their very presence.
The Devoted Vajra Praise: The praise says:
"All the noble ones rejoice. Visualize a vajra wheel atop the head of the deity, revolving in the sky.
Beneath the seat are two golden wheels. Next is the Mother of the Vajra Family, followed by Mahācakra-vajrī. For the root confession mudrā:
interlace the thumbs and ring fingers inwardly; join the thumbs, middle fingers, and little fingers together.
Like a wheel, a triangle, and blazing light, with dhyāna and prajñā at the crown, grant me joy!
Having now bound the protection according to the ritual, and for all omissions and violations of the samaya,
I confess all transgressions of the four periods through the mantra of the Secret Holder Soma-vajra.
Next, clap the vajra-palms. The mantra for causing the assembly of noble ones to rejoice is as follows:
With both hands holding the rosary, bring it to the crown of the head and place it at the heart.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajraguhyarājasamayai hūṃ. The mantra for holding the rosary is:
Contemplate the wondrous bodhicitta as a perfectly luminous and pure lunar disc.
The secret syllable-gateway of the letter A:
whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, may the light of purple-golden hue always appear before me;
with body and mind unmoving, I shall observe all phenomena with equanimity.
In a low voice, audible only to oneself, neither too slow nor too hurried,
while reciting at that time, one should single-mindedly focus on departing from the maṇḍala and pay homage to all the noble assemblies. The verse says:
I entreat you to descend into samādhi; do not contradict your original vow, but fulfill your unerring activities throughout the world for a time.
I pray that the noble assembly may return to perfect nirvāṇa, yet continue to vibrate the vajra bell.
The mantra is as follows:
"Advancing slowly and with composure, one enters while reciting the syllable HŪṂ.
Having completed the clear visualization, when wishing to depart, one again performs the Universal Offering."
Next, the Mantra of the Mother of the Sections:
I now, for the sake of all beings, Seeking the fruit of Bodhi,
pray that the Great Holy Honored One May accomplish my recitation in full measure.
Constantly bind the seal of the Family Mother (*kulamātṛmudrā*). Empower with the hundred-syllable mantra to cause the deity to rejoice.
Rotate counter-clockwise within the fire-court to perform the release of the great seal (*mahāmudrā*), reciting the verse as follows:
The Tathāgatas of the present age, the world-saving Bodhisattvas,
and those who maintain the Mahāyāna teachings without interruption— having reached the stage of supreme wisdom—
may the assembly of noble devas and deities please grant their definitive witness to me.
Each should remain as they find comfort; thereafter, out of compassion, descend once more to recite the verses for dismissal.
Having thus performed this supreme benefit, it is bestowed upon all sentient beings.
May all the noble ones return to their native lands; Shaking the bells, do not fail your great vows.
Next, perform the arousal of the bodhicitta; Then, follow the standard ritual for the three-family protection of the body and the confession of transgressions.
Thereafter, proceed as you wish, whether walking or sitting in meditation.

The Ritual for the Accomplishment of Siddhi through the Practice of Mahācakra-vajra and its Offerings, composed on an auspicious morning in the seventh month of the year Jisi (the 2nd year of Kwan’en).
